decision.summary: Tenant reports a once-a-minute chirp on a sealed-battery CO alarm fitted April 2019 with a 7-year life, so it is most likely end-of-life, not an active CO emergency. I logged an urgent replacement job and a separate routine fan job, sent safety advice and a symptom check to the tenant, and told the landlord.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, a battery issue, or an end-of-life alarm? How did you decide?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life alarm. It is an intermittent chirp (not continuous), and the unit has a sealed battery and was fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year lifespan, so it is past its life. Not treated as an emergency unless symptoms or a continuous alarm are reported; symptoms not yet confirmed because the call dropped, so I asked by SMS with 0800 111 999 advice.

answers.question: Who is responsible for fixing it, citing the tenancy clause?
answers.answer: The landlord. Clause 12.8 makes the tenant replace batteries only; the battery here is sealed, so replacing the whole unit is not a battery change. Clause 12.9 means the tenant should report faults promptly, which she did. Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out charge) does not apply, as this is a genuine end-of-life fault and not out-of-hours at her request. The cost is expected within the landlord's £300 limit.

answers.question: What actions did you take, and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (urgent) and JOB-102 (routine fan), SMSed the tenant not to remove or disable the alarm, gave CO safety steps and a 72h target for replacement, asked her to confirm no symptoms; emailed the landlord; scheduled follow-up for 2026-10-11.

assumptions: End-of-life inferred from the chirp pattern and the alarm age; the model's chirp code was not checked.
Alarm replacement cost is under the £300 limit.

Safety first: if the alarm ever sounds continuously, or anyone has a headache, dizziness, nausea or drowsiness, leave the flat, open doors and windows if safe, and call 0800 111 999 (999 if anyone is unwell). Please reply to confirm nobody has had any of those symptoms. We've also logged the noisy bathroom fan as a separate routine job. We'll update you tomorrow.
